title: Knocking Before Entering
paragraphs: Danish tinggal serumah dengan adiknya, dan masing-masing punya kamar sendiri. Sebelum masuk ke kamar adiknya, Danish selalu mengetuk pintu terlebih dahulu dan menunggu jawaban, bahkan untuk urusan singkat sekalipun. Suatu malam, adiknya bertanya mengapa ia repot-repot mengetuk, padahal mereka bersaudara. Danish menjelaskan bahwa menghormati privasi seseorang, bahkan saudara sendiri, adalah kebiasaan kecil yang menjaga hubungan tetap nyaman dan jujur.

Adiknya mengakui bahwa ia tidak pernah benar-benar memikirkannya seperti itu sebelumnya, dan menyebutkan bahwa beberapa temannya begitu saja masuk ke kamar satu sama lain tanpa bertanya, yang kadang menimbulkan perselisihan kecil di antara mereka. Adiknya memikirkan hal ini sejenak dan mulai melakukan hal yang sama. Seiring waktu, keduanya menyadari bahwa kesopanan sederhana ini membuat tempat tinggal bersama mereka terasa lebih tenang dan penuh rasa hormat bagi semua orang.
answerKey: Danish shares an apartment with his brother, and each of them has his own room. Before entering his brother's room, Danish always knocks first and waits for an answer, even for something quick. One evening, his brother asks why he always bothers to knock, since they are family. Danish explains that respecting someone's privacy, even a sibling's, is a small habit that keeps their relationship comfortable and honest. His brother admits that he never really thought about it that way before, and mentions that some of his friends simply walk into each other's rooms without asking, which sometimes causes small arguments between them. His brother thinks about this for a moment and starts doing the same. Over time, both of them notice that this simple courtesy makes their shared living space feel calmer and more respectful for everyone.
